Blackburn with Darwen's population increased by around 7,300 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population passed 150,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Blackburn with Darwen increased by 4.9%, from just under 147,500 in 2011 to around 154,700 in 2021.

The population here increased at a similar rate to the overall population of the North West (5.2%), but by a smaller percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Blackburn with Darwen was home to around 8.1 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 7.7 in 2011. This area was among the top 45% most densely populated English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was similar in Blackburn with Darwen to the North West as a whole

Median age in Blackburn with Darwen

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Blackburn with Darwen increased by one year, from 35 to 36 years of age.

This area had a lower average (median) age than the North West as a whole in 2021 (40 years) and a lower average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 50 to 64 years rose by just under 3,000 (an increase of 12.0%), while the number of residents aged 4 years and under fell by just over 1,200 (10.8% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 50 and 64 years increased by 1.1 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Blackburn with Darwen stood out from other areas for housing

The percentage of households in the social rented sector increased in Blackburn with Darwen, but fell across the North West.

In Blackburn with Darwen, the percentage of households in the social rented sector rose from 18.1% in 2011 to 18.8% in 2021. During the same period, the regional percentage fell from 18.3% to 17.6%.

Private renting in Blackburn with Darwen increased from 15.7% to 20.2%, while the rate of home ownership decreased from 64.2% to 60.5%.

The rate of social renting in Blackburn with Darwen increased by 0.7 percentage points

Ethnic groups in Blackburn with Darwen

In 2021, 35.7% of Blackburn with Darwen residents identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category, up from 28.1% in 2011. The 7.5 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the North West, the percentage of people from the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" ethnic group increased from 6.2% to 8.4%, while across England the percentage increased from 7.8% to 9.6%.

In 2021, 60.4% of people in Blackburn with Darwen identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 69.2% in 2011), while 1.7% identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category (compared with 1.2% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Other" category ("Arab" or "Any other ethnic group") increased from 0.8% in 2011 to 1.4% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.

Disability in Blackburn with Darwen

Blackburn with Darwen saw the North West's second-largest percentage-point fall in the proportion of residents who were identified as disabled and limited a little (from 11.6% in 2011 to 10.3% in 2021). These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

Across the region, only Pendle saw a greater fall in the proportion of residents who were identified as disabled and limited a little (from 11.5% to 9.8%).

Across the North West, the proportion of residents who were identified as disabled and limited a little remained 10.7%, while the proportion in nearby Chorley increased from 10.0% to 10.7%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a little in Blackburn with Darwen decreased by 1.3 percentage points

Blackburn with Darwen residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 124,000 Blackburn with Darwen residents said they were born in England. This represented 80.2% of the local population. The figure has risen from around 122,200 in 2011, which at the time represented 82.8% of Blackburn with Darwen's population.

Pakistan was the next most represented, with around 9,600 Blackburn with Darwen residents reporting this country of birth (6.2%). This figure was up from around 6,500 in 2011, which at the time represented 4.4% of the population of Blackburn with Darwen.

The number of Blackburn with Darwen residents born in India rose from around 6,200 in 2011 (4.2% of the local population) to just under 6,300 in 2021 (4.1%).

In 2021, 80.2% of Blackburn with Darwen residents reported their country of birth as England

Religion in Blackburn with Darwen

In 2021, 35.0% of Blackburn with Darwen residents described themselves as Muslim, up from 27.0% in 2011. The rise of 8.0 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Blackburn with Darwen. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the North West, the percentage of residents who described themselves as Muslim increased from 5.1% to 7.6%, while across England the percentage increased from 5.0% to 6.7%.

In 2021, 38.0% of people in Blackburn with Darwen described themselves as Christian (down from 52.6%), while 21.1% reported having "No religion" (up from 13.8% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

In 2021, 35.0% of usual residents in Blackburn with Darwen described themselves as Muslim

Health in Blackburn with Darwen

In 2021, 43.6% of Blackburn with Darwen residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 40.1% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 34.0% to 33.5%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Blackburn with Darwen residents describing their health as "very bad" remained 1.9%, while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 7.0% to 5.9%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in very good health in Blackburn with Darwen increased by 3.5 percentage points

National identity in Blackburn with Darwen

In 2021, 8.3% of Blackburn with Darwen residents did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. This figure increased from 5.6% in 2011.

In 2021, 1.4% of residents identified with a UK and non-UK national identity, compared with 0.7% in 2011. The percentage of residents in Blackburn with Darwen that identified as "British only" increased from 27.7% to 64.4%.

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was greater in Blackburn with Darwen (2.7 percentage points) than across the North West (2.3 percentage points, from 4.7% to 7.1%). Across England, the percentage increased by 1.7 percentage points, from 8.2% to 10.0%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Blackburn with Darwen increased by 2.7 percentage points

Unpaid care in Blackburn with Darwen

In 2021, 4.0% of Blackburn with Darwen residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 6.8% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, around 1 in 40 people (2.5%) reported providing between 20 and 49 hours of unpaid care each week, compared with 2.1% in 2011. The proportion of Blackburn with Darwen residents (aged five years and over) that provided at least 50 hours of weekly unpaid care decreased from 3.6% to 3.4%.

This area had the region’s third lowest proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care. Across the region, only Manchester (3.4%) and Salford (3.8%) had a lower proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Blackburn with Darwen decreased by 2.8 percentage points

Family in Blackburn with Darwen

In 2021, 6.8% of Blackburn with Darwen households included a couple with only non-dependent children. This figure increased from 6.4% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in five households (21.9%) included a couple with dependent children, compared with 22.2% in 2011. The percentage of single-family households including a couple without children decreased from 14.9% to 13.5%.

Blackburn with Darwen saw the North West's joint third-largest rise (alongside Bolton and Rochdale) in the percentage of households including a couple with only non-dependent children.

The percentage of households including a couple with only non-dependent children in Blackburn with Darwen increased by 0.5 percentage points

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of Blackburn with Darwen residents aged 16 years and over, 37.8% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 33.6% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in two people (45.4%) said they were married or in a registered civil partnership, compared with 47.8% in 2011. The percentage of adults in Blackburn with Darwen that had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership decreased from 9.0% to 8.5%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership was greater in Blackburn with Darwen (4.2 percentage points) than across the North West (3.8 percentage points, from 35.6% to 39.4%). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.3 percentage points, from 34.6% to 37.9%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Blackburn with Darwen increased by 4.2 percentage points

Employment in Blackburn with Darwen

Of Blackburn with Darwen residents aged 16 years and over, 51.5% said they were employed (excluding full-time students) in 2021, a similar percentage as in 2011 (51.6%).

In 2021, just under 1 in 30 people (3.2%) said they were unemployed, compared with 4.9% in 2011. The percentage of retired Blackburn with Darwen residents decreased from 18.9% to 17.8%.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed fell from 54.2% to 53.7% across the North West. Across England, the percentage fell from 56.5% to 55.7%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) in Blackburn with Darwen decreased by 0.1 percentage points

Change in work hours

In 2021, 9.2% of Blackburn with Darwen residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked 15 hours or less per week. This figure increased from 8.5% in 2011.

In 2021, around 1 in 15 people (6.7%) said they worked over 49 hours per week, compared with 8.5% in 2011. The percentage of adults in employment working 31 to 48 hours per week increased from 60.1% to 60.9%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week in Blackburn with Darwen (0.7 percentage points) was similar to the increase across the North West (0.5 percentage points, from 9.1% to 9.6%). Across England, the percentage increased by 0.6 percentage points, from 9.7% to 10.3%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in Blackburn with Darwen increased by 0.7 percentage points
